Definition: of Hebrew origin (H7927); Sychem (i.e. Shekem), the name of a Canaanite and of a place in Palestine:--Sychem.
BiblicalUsage: Sychem is the name of a man and of the town, and Stephen names the town: the patriarchs were carried over into Sychem, and laid in the sepulchre that Abraham bought for a sum of money of the sons of Emmor the father of Sychem. The burial ground joins the patriarchs to the place.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Sychem holds the patriarchs together: bought by Abraham, and the resting place of his sons.
